Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Momu-Fas is a nominative-accusative language. There is no overt absolutive marker.
curated_comment: Momu-Fas (fass1245, ISO fqs, Trans-New Guinea, PNG) is a nominative-accusative language. The original annotation incorrectly interpreted the oblique/object marker =m (documented in Honeyman 2016) as an ergative marker, leading to spurious ergative values (GB409_2=1, GB409_6-7=1, etc.) in the source xlsx. PDF verification of Honeyman (2016) confirms that =m marks objects/obliques in a NOM-ACC system, not a subject-A in an ERG-ABS system. Blake (2007), an earlier description of the same language (also known as Fas), likewise shows no ergative alignment. All 24 features are correctly 0. Glottocode fass1245 is correct; the previously proposed momu1235 does not exist in Glottolog. File moved to non_ergative/ after PDF verification.
